steps.name: Legion Commander
steps.text: Consul Gladiia, is it in your opinion that the issue does not lie with the battle itself?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Correct. What you see before you is a projection of the battle plan. If anyone here notices a flaw I haven't, I'd expect it to be pointed out.

steps.name: Legion Commander
steps.text: No, I have no objections to the battle plan. It was the most suitable one, given what we knew at the time.

steps.name: Legion Commander
steps.text: However, I would like your opinion on what we knew at the time.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I have to admit that Ægir's knowledge of the Seaborn back then was deeply flawed. As such...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What are they trying to say?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Still not used to their way of thinking, are you? You never did like thinking much, even back home.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: They mean no ill will. They're simply seeking the truth they need.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Identify every flaw and question all perfections. The most heated debates will uncover truth in its full beauty and reveal the right way forward.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Just leave it to Swordfish.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: If you don't want to listen, just take a nap.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...In conclusion, our greatest error when designing the warfare five years ago was failing to make allowance for flaws in our knowledge.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Until every last truth of Terra is revealed, we must admit that our understanding of the Seaborn will remain flawed. Our warfare design must reflect this revelation.

steps.name: Legion Commander
steps.text: I concur. Your conclusion should be incorporated into our future battle plans.

steps.name: Legion Commander
steps.text: It has been an honor to reflect upon this critical battle and reach a fruitful conclusion with you.

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: That said, the battle five years ago is not our only concern.

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: We have more pressing issues to worry about.

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: Your physical examination has revealed mutations that cannot be ignored. The same goes for Skadi and Laurentina.

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: I do not doubt your loyalty, but we need to know how assimilation by Seaborn genes will affect your behavior.

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: Apologies for my candor.

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: Milliarium will soon identify the locations of the remaining nests. Then, the Seaborn will be driven out by Class IV weapons, opening up a Waterway.

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: Is there any possibility that the Abyssal Hunters will become an enemy of Ægir, and of yourselves?
Hunters out of control pose a greater risk to Ægir than the Seaborn.
The Abyssal Hunters are the flipside of Ægir. Created in Ægir's most despicable attempt at salvation, they are now both feared and pitied by their creators.

options: Abyssal Hunter Ulpianus, I presume?
Shouldn't you be down there too?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You're much calmer than I expected. And you know who I am.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: It seems Gladiia has built a relationship on land with more than just the one doctor.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I've never seen you in any of the operations. You're not an Inquisitor, nor an Islander.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The doctor from Rhodes Island brought you to Ægir, but kept your identity a secret.

options: I'm just Kal'tsit's colleague.
I'm also from Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You may introduce yourself however you like.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: However, the point is that you can help the Hunters.

options: Why don't you just go to Skadi?
Why don't you just go to Specter?
Why don't you just go to Gladiia?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: This is not her forte.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You mean Laurentina?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: This is not her forte.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Now is not the time.

options: You don't trust the Hunters?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: On the contrary. I do trust them. But I also know them all too well.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Skadi acts before thinking. Laurentina has not been lucid for long. Gladiia will inevitably be the one to make decisions.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I've already shared much of what I know with her. She should be on guard. She knows the potential restrictions, but nevertheless decided to return to Ægir.

spans.text: I've already shared much of what I know with her. She
be on guard. She knows the potential restrictions, but nevertheless decided to return to Ægir.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Overeager to return to a familiar environment, she is oblivious to the fact that she has placed herself in the spotlight, where all that can and cannot be trusted have the power to scrutinize her.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Now is not the best time for the Abyssal Hunters to come home. Their decision is a big gamble.

options: Why did you sneak into the city, then?
Sounds like you care about them, after all.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Gladiia and the others are not in a good situation.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: They underwent modifications, but unlike me, they were not part of the Abyssal Hunter project's core research. Explaining the changes in their bodies will be difficult for them.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I'll pass on some information to you, and I'll need you to help Gladiia if necessary. Convey my warning to her later.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: As for the rest—

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: May I say I few things?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: ...Blandus. He's here too?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Blandus?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Isn't this just like the old days? You and Ulpianus used to get into arguments with the research staff while I was napping.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Your comments would be much appreciated, Advisor.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: You flatter me, Consul.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I was the technical advisor for the Abyssal Hunter project, responsible for the gene splicing research used in the modification process.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: In other words, at this exact moment and in this exact place, I am the leading authority on Abyssal Hunters.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Gladiia, Laurentina, and Skadi have been fighting on dry land too frequently and for too long. It is indeed cause for concern regarding their physical condition.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: As such, your concerns are not without reason. But my answer is this:

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: No—

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: They will not become Seaborn.
The hall goes silent.
Blandus clears his throat.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Let me try to explain this in layman's terms.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Under ordinary circumstances, Seaborn genes exhibit abnormal dominance and will irreversibly overwrite any preexisting traits in their host.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: In Abyssal Hunters, however, we have managed to extend the timeline of this process until it far exceeds the natural lifespan of any given Hunter.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Furthermore, the Academy of Technology made a critical breakthrough, allowing us to implant an 'auto-adaptive junction' in all the Hunters before their deployment to eradicate the Firstborn.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The auto-adaptive junction was implanted at the splice point between human and Seaborn DNA to assist the Hunters in more closely monitoring their Seaborn genes.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: If the Seaborn genes exhibited abnormal dominance, the junction would signal the body to resist their attempt at taking over.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: While there has undoubtedly been some degree of decay of their auto-adaptive junctions after five years without maintenance, the changes they've undergone remain well within acceptable ranges.

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: So you say, Advisor, but there is a record of a failed auto-adaptive junction surgery in the Abyssal Hunter Lab archives.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: ...That was Ulpianus.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: The archives should also note that multiple clinical trials have demonstrated that the incident did not produce any adverse effects.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: For this, I gladly take full responsibility and will answer any queries.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Now that the Abyssal Hunters have returned to Ægir, their condition will be under control.

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: Am I to infer that you already have an effective means to contain their mutation?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: There is an Abyssal Hunter Lab in the city we can reactivate. I will personally perform maintenance on their auto-adaptive junctions.

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: What of Ulpianus?

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: How can we be sure that the Hunter who has refused to return to Ægir will not become Seaborn?

steps.name: Academy of Science Researcher
steps.text: Or that what we fear hasn't already happened?

options: Sounds like you've just become the target.
Sounds like you're pretty dangerous.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: It's only natural they would be skeptical.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: It is both human nature and a hard-learned lesson to be wary of what you cannot control.

options: They're not the only ones suspicious of you.
I'm equally curious about your motivations.
Did you really come out of concern for the Hunters?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Before the sinking of the Stultifera, I shared my discovery with Gladiia: there is more than one entity like Ishar'mla amongst the Seaborn, those known as Firstborn.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The Firstborn are stirring. It, or rather They, are about to awaken.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I don't know how many or how soon... but it's close. Too close.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: This is why the Seaborn have begun migrating towards land. I've ventured into many nests recently, and as a whole, they are feeling a sense of crisis.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Perhaps not even the ocean contains enough nourishment for the awakening of a new god. Will it become another Profound Silence for the land, or another calamity for the seas?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The great migration almost perfectly coincides with Ægir's Waterway Program. One can only speculate about Milliarium's role in all this.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Is that not reason enough for me to visit this city?

steps.name: Academy of Technology Researcher
steps.text: The Seaborn have proliferated independently, driven by their instincts. But they came from the Firstborn, and cannot defy their fundamental nature.

steps.name: Academy of Technology Researcher
steps.text: In other words, even if the death of the Firstborn failed to halt their evolution, it should not have caused the rapid emergence of new, previously undocumented traits.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I believe I already addressed that in my report.

steps.name: Academy of Technology Researcher
steps.text: Yes, the Multiple Firstborn hypothesis. A logical enough explanation, but that is exactly why I am skeptical of Ulpianus.

steps.name: Academy of Technology Researcher
steps.text: Our well-laid plans ended in failure. The three surviving Hunters washed ashore on unfamiliar land, before being reunited with the Hunter who was last to leave the nest.

steps.name: Academy of Technology Researcher
steps.text: The information Ulpianus brought—that there are more than one Firstborn in the ocean—is more than shocking, it's highly 'effective.'

steps.name: Academy of Technology Researcher
steps.text: Effective in explaining why the Seaborn's actions have become more disruptive despite your success with the mission objective. Effective in addressing all our questions.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And why does that make you skeptical?

steps.name: Academy of Technology Researcher
steps.text: Because it's an answer so perfect that it's either the incontrovertible truth, or was designed specifically to put our questions to rest.

steps.name: Academy of Technology Researcher
steps.text: Whether or not to believe the information he gave you will have an enormous impact on our warfare design.

steps.name: Academy of Technology Researcher
steps.text: If Ulpianus lives, then the most effective way to verify his claims would be to track him down, perhaps even question him directly.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: You have been quiet, Advisor Blandus.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Do you have anything to add regarding Ulpianus?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: You were once students under the same mentor, and it was your trust in him that led you to join the Abyssal Hunter project despite your reservations.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: But I also trust your knowledge and ethics as an Ægir. You need not recuse yourself.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: All I can say, Madame Consul, is that I can be accountable for every word I say here at this tribunal.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I will not intentionally put forward a hypothesis in his favor, nor will I make any conjectures that could hurt him.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: That is all.

options: Sounds like you two are pretty close.
I guess even a loner has friends.

steps.text: Ulpianus does not answer. The questioning continues, but Blandus says no more. Suddenly, he looks up towards you, as though he's sensed something.
You meet his weary gaze across the length of the Sophontheatrum.
He seems to have noticed something. The consul next to him and several other Ægir catch that peculiar moment, and some of them follow his gaze.

options: Em...

steps.text: You look to your side and find the seat empty.

options: Don't mind me. Just a landlubber here to watch.
Sorry, am I interrupting?
Do I need to speak?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The tribunal has arrived at an adequate conclusion.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Gladiia, Skadi, Laurentina, and the rest of the Abyssal Hunters have made tremendous sacrifices and contributions to Ægir.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: It is a blessing for Ægir that new ideas continue to emerge from their knowledge and experience even after five years.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: They have demonstrated that they are both innocent and safe, and that their return at this stage of the Waterway Program is not a threat, but a reassurance.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Yet now our attention turns to another of the surviving Hunters, Ulpianus.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: He has concealed his movements for reasons unknown, and has attempted to influence the other Hunters. Both actions clearly contravene his duty.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Based on our present information, we are unable to determine his motives, goals, or even whether he still qualifies as Ægir.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Ulpianus must be found. If his intentions are indeed benign, as Gladiia claims, our suspicions must be cleared through proper questioning.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Those whose questions have been answered may now leave. Those whose questions have not may continue their inquiries.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Do you have anything to add, Consul Gladiia?
The coral-shaped terminal at the center of the Sophontheatrum slowly closes and sinks into the ground. The space is now flat and empty, like a stage ready for a new play.
Gladiia stands alone on it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I have told you all I know.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I have no objections to the tribunal's conclusion, nor to the suspicions cast upon Ulpianus.
People begin to file out, many turning to nod towards Gladiia as they reach the exit.
The remaining audience continue to ask questions, and Gladiia responds to each one, whether she is able to answer or not.
The water caustics cast by the dome weave a picture of light and shadow with the ring of light surrounding the space, dancing on Gladiia's expressionless face.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Even as an Ægir, I find this hard to understand sometimes.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They fling words at her like spears one moment, then thank her for her contributions the next.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: They're sincere, you know. Science requires people to separate facts from feelings, and they're good at it.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I know. I'm just... *sigh* Never mind.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: As for Captain Ulpianus, all they have are suspicions. Swordfish, the Doctor, Kal'tsit... someone will think of a way.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What next?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: We wait for Swordfish. Which, unfortunately, will take a while. *sigh*...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You're sighing too?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: She used to visit the Sophontheatrum to watch plays whenever there wasn't a mission. Sometimes I went with her.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Captain Gladiia...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: She's fairly well-versed in the arts. Her mother's influence, supposedly.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Unlike everyone else, however, she liked the highest, furthest seats, so I would always end up having to sit apart from her.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: For her, keeping the distance helps filter out the noise. Ignoring some of the finer details makes it easier for her to fully immerse herself in the story.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Right now, though, she's the one at center stage.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: She’s lost her accustomed sense of distance, becoming the subject of judgment, scrutiny, and discussion. No one in her position can remain unperturbed.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm starting to get why I sighed.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Because only now does it really feel like we're back.
